findings.problem: status is a public String field, allowing any arbitrary value (e.g. "sent", "pending", "foo", "DEAD") instead of a closed domain enum
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can place BudgetWorkflow into a status that the domain never defines, breaking invariant reasoning across the entire codebase
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with a private `status: BudgetStatus` enum with only the valid domain variants, exposing only methods that preserve invariants

findings.problem: `is_validated: bool` is a raw boolean lifecycle flag that carries no domain meaning and allows illegal combinations (e.g. is_validated=true with invalid status)
findings.failure_mode: Boolean flags cannot encode the lifecycle ordering or mutually exclusive states; callers can construct logically inconsistent workflows that compile fine
findings.fix: Replace `is_validated: bool` and `is_sent: bool` with a single `BudgetState` typestate enum that encodes the legal lifecycle (e.g. Created, Validated, Sent, Archived) and makes illegal transitions compile errors

findings.problem: `is_sent: bool` is a raw boolean lifecycle flag that should be part of the typestate enum, not a separate field
findings.failure_mode: Separate bools for lifecycle flags allow states like is_validated=false and is_sent=true, which violates the workflow invariant that validation must precede sending
findings.fix: Merge into a single typestate enum; the transition from Validated to Sent becomes the only way to reach the Sent state

findings.problem: No typed domain constructor; `id: String` is a raw primitive with no validation, no newtype wrapper, and no fallible constructor to reject invalid IDs at the boundary
findings.failure_mode: Any raw string (empty, whitespace, malformed) becomes a valid BudgetWorkflow ID in the core, pushing all validation into every caller instead of enforcing it at the parse boundary
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct BudgetId(String)` or `NonEmptyTrimmedString` with a fallible `fn new(s: String) -> Result<BudgetId, InvalidId>` constructor; make BudgetWorkflow fields private with a constructor that envariants

findings.problem: `mark_sent` mutates the struct in place (`item.status = "sent".to_string(); item.is_sent = true;`) instead of returning a new immutable value or using an enum transition
findings.failure_mode: The function mutates owned data instead of being a pure function that computes a new state; the String assignment allocates and the mutation bypasses any lifecycle invariants
findings.fix: Define `mark_sent(state: BudgetState) -> Result<BudgetState, TransitionError>` as a pure function on the typestate enum, returning the next legal state or a typed domain error

findings.problem: `"sent".to_string()` performs an unnecessary heap allocation in what should be a pure, allocation-free domain transition; the string literal is never a domain value
findings.failure_mode: Every call to `mark_sent` allocates a new String on the heap even though the status value is a known constant; this is a performance leak in the hot path
findings.fix: Use an enum variant instead of a String for status; the domain transition becomes a pure value computation with zero allocation

findings.problem: All fields of `BudgetWorkflow` are `pub`, so any caller can construct the struct with any combination of values, including logically inconsistent ones
findings.failure_mode: The type system provides zero guarantee that a BudgetWorkflow instance represents a legal workflow state; all correctness depends on caller discipline
findings.fix: Make all fields private and provide a fallible constructor (or builder) that enforces domain invariants; expose only state-safe accessors

findings.problem: `sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>` is a bare Option that allows the sent timestamp to be present even when the budget is not in a sent state (since is_validated/is_sent are separate bools)
findings.failure_mode: The timestamp can be set or unset independently of the lifecycle state, creating inconsistency: a non-sent budget can have a sent timestamp, or a sent budget can lack one
findings.fix: Tie the timestamp to the typestate enum: the Sent variant carries the `u64` timestamp; non-sent variants carry none, making illegal states unrepresentable
